gap: No result ChatGPT got states that, on Cable Matters' own product page, its active 48 Gbps extension (Product ID 300046) comes only in a 6.6 ft size, claims ARC but never eARC, and needs current TV firmware and the TV's enhanced HDMI mode (Input Signal Plus / HDMI Ultra HD Deep Color / Enhanced Format) for 8K on 8K TVs and for LG's 4K@120Hz and 8K modes. ChatGPT's 'up to 16.4 ft' card is the cable's 'extend an 8K run by 5 m' claim, not a length you can buy.
standout_why: I read the cited Cable Matters page (pc-1330-142) and its twin (pc-1330-139), plus the cited itechguides.com guide. The Cable Matters page already gives the cable's direction (female end to the source, reversed 'will not work'), the optional Micro-B power, the 6.6 ft size and the firmware note, so this finding is partly on a cited page. ChatGPT's answer misread it as 'Up to 16.4 ft' and left out the missing eARC claim. Itechguides covers certification labels and eARC failures in general terms and names a StarTech booster with no ARC/eARC, but not these two cables. The cited UGREEN HD151 page (bestways.com) returned HTTP 429 twice, so I couldn't check what it says.
decides: This changes the picks for soundbar and long-run setups. Anyone who needs eARC passthrough (TV to soundbar or AVR) should not count on the Cable Matters active extension, because its page only claims ARC. Anyone who needs more than 6.6 ft can't buy a longer one from that page. For 4K120 or 8K, check the TV's firmware and enhanced-HDMI setting before blaming the cable. Neither extension has an Ultra High Speed certification label on a page I could open. HDMI LA makes that label mandatory for Ultra High Speed cables, so the 'certified single cable' advice ChatGPT got from iTechGuides still holds over either extension.

findings.product: Cable Matters 48Gbps Active 8K HDMI Extension Cable (300046)
findings.label: Direction (which end goes where)
findings.value: Works one way only. The female connector must go to the source device and the male plug to the display. Reversed, it 'will not work'.
findings.source_title: 48Gbps Active 8K HDMI Extension Cable, Male to Female | Cable Matters
findings.note: Product page FAQ: 'This cable is NOT bi-directional' and 'The female connector must be connected to the source device.' The cited page pc-1330-142 has the same text.

findings.product: Cable Matters 48Gbps Active 8K HDMI Extension Cable (300046)
findings.label: Lengths offered
findings.source_title: 48Gbps Active 8K HDMI Extension Cable | Cable Matters
findings.note: The Size dropdown lists only 6.6 ft. The page copy says 'Extend an 8K cable run by 5 meters (16.4 feet)', which is where ChatGPT's 'Up to 16.4 ft' came from. That is a reach claim, not a length you can buy.

findings.product: Cable Matters 48Gbps Active 8K HDMI Extension Cable (300046)
findings.label: Audio return support stated
findings.value: ARC only ('Fully compatible with HDMI ARC (Audio Return Channel)'). eARC is not mentioned.
findings.source_title: 48Gbps Active 8K HDMI Extension Cable | Cable Matters
findings.note: Read the full spec and FAQ. VRR is not mentioned either. The page lists Dolby Atmos and DTS:X over ARC.

findings.product: Cable Matters 48Gbps Active 8K HDMI Extension Cable (300046)
findings.label: TV-side requirements
findings.value: LG 8K and 4K@120Hz TVs need the latest TV firmware for those modes. 8K TVs need 'Input Signal Plus / HDMI Ultra HD Deep Color / Enhanced Format' turned on to show 8K. Cable Matters also says to update the GPU driver for 8K and 120 Hz.
findings.source_title: 48Gbps Active 8K HDMI Extension Cable | Cable Matters
findings.note: From the page's Important Notes section.

findings.product: Cable Matters 48Gbps Active 8K HDMI Extension Cable (300046)
findings.label: Power
findings.value: Micro-B USB power port with a USB cable included. Power is 'optional but recommended, especially for longer distances or 8K signals'.
findings.source_title: 48Gbps Active 8K HDMI Extension Cable | Cable Matters

findings.product: Cable Matters 48Gbps Active 8K HDMI Extension Cable (300046)
findings.label: Devices the maker names
findings.value: PS4 Pro, PlayStation 5, Xbox One, Xbox Series X/S, 'and other high-definition game consoles and AV equipment'. No exclusions listed.
findings.source_title: 48Gbps Active 8K HDMI Extension Cable, Male to Female | Cable Matters
findings.note: No Ultra High Speed HDMI certification is shown anywhere on the page.

findings.label: Ultra High Speed HDMI certification rule
findings.value: Every Ultra High Speed cable model must pass testing at an HDMI Forum Authorized Testing Center and carry the certification label on each package. The label can be scanned with a standard QR code app.
findings.source_title: Ultra High Speed HDMI Cable | HDMI.org
findings.note: The page says nothing about extension or male-to-female cables either way.

findings.label: Male-to-female extensions can be certified
findings.value: Canare says its HDM***U series 'has qualified for The Ultra High Speed HDMI Certification Program'. Its HDM003E-FM (0.3 m) and HDM02E-FM (2.0 m) male-to-female models are rated '4K30p and up to 10.2 Gbps' only.
findings.note: This is Canare's Japan/global page. It doesn't say whether these are sold in the US.

unsourced: UGREEN HD151 maximum total length with an extra male cable: search snippets quote UGREEN listings capping the male cable at 2 m (30AWG) with the 1 m HD151, or at 1 m with the 6.6 ft model, for 8K@60Hz / 4K@240Hz. The UGREEN US, UK and EU stores (searched with storecheck.py) don't list the HD151. Amazon B08YWBVRVH, B08YX5QMVP and B0GX18SQL7 returned 503. Datablitz, pclan and bestways returned 429. A direct curl needed approval. I found no UGREEN manual or PDF.
UGREEN HD151 eARC, VRR and device list from UGREEN itself: only a third-party affiliate page (thebestkit.pages.dev) states them.
Whether the UGREEN HD151 or Cable Matters 300046 has an HDMI LA Ultra High Speed certification label: neither page I could open shows one, and I found no HDMI LA lookup entry.
Prices for both candidates: the Cable Matters page showed no price, UGREEN US doesn't list the HD151, and Amazon was walled.
